nodes.summary: The set of binomials `x^a - x^b` whose exponent vectors have the same sufficient statistic, `∑ a(x) T(x) = ∑ b(x) T(x)`. Up to a monomial factor these are the monomial differences `x^{f⁺} - x^{f⁻}` with `∑ f(x) T(x) = 0` of Diaconis–Sturmfels (1998), equation (3.1), since `x^a - x^b = x^{a ⊓ b} (x^{a - a ⊓ b} - x^{b - a ⊓ b})`.
nodes.title: Binomials of a toric model

nodes.summary: Let `T : X → ℕ^d` be the sufficient statistic of a discrete exponential family on a set of cells `X`, and `k` any field. A family of integer moves `f_i : X → ℤ` is a Markov basis for `T` (each move lies in the lattice `∑_x f_i(x) T(x) = 0`, and any two tables of counts with the same sufficient statistic are joined by steps `± f_i` that keep all counts nonnegative) if and only if the binomials `x^{f_i⁺} - x^{f_i⁻}`…
nodes.title: Fundamental theorem of Markov bases

nodes.summary: Moves `f_i : X → ℤ` form a Markov basis for the statistic `T` when (a) each `f_i` lies in the lattice of moves, `∑_x f_i(x) T(x) = 0`, and (b) any two tables `g, g'` with the same sufficient statistic are joined by a sequence of steps `± f_i` through tables of nonnegative counts (Diaconis–Sturmfels 1998, Definition (1.5)).
nodes.title: Markov basis

nodes.summary: `∑_x f(x) T(x) = 0` holds if and only if `f⁺` and `f⁻` have the same sufficient statistic.
nodes.title: Lattice condition in terms of positive and negative parts

nodes.summary: If `h = g ± f_i` with `g, h ≥ 0`, then `x^g - x^h = ∓ x^c (x^{f_i⁺} - x^{f_i⁻})` for some monomial `x^c`, so it lies in the ideal generated by the move binomials (Diaconis–Sturmfels 1998, proof of Theorem 3.1).
nodes.title: A single move changes `x^g` by a monomial multiple of a move binomial

nodes.summary: `x^a - x^b ∈ I_T` if and only if `∑ a(x) T(x) = ∑ b(x) T(x)` (Diaconis–Sturmfels 1998, Section 3.1, the observation before Theorem 3.1).
nodes.title: A binomial lies in the toric ideal iff its exponents have the same statistic

nodes.summary: A move binomial lies in the toric ideal iff the move lies in the lattice of moves.
nodes.title: A move binomial lies in the toric ideal iff the move lies in the lattice of moves

nodes.summary: `x^{f⁺} - x^{f⁻}` (Diaconis–Sturmfels 1998, Theorem 3.1).
nodes.title: Binomial of a move

nodes.summary: If `g ↦ h` is a step, so is `g + c ↦ h + c`.
nodes.title: Moves are translation invariant

nodes.summary: `f⁻ ↦ f⁻ + f = f⁺` is a step of the chain.
nodes.title: Each move joins its negative part to its positive part

nodes.summary: A step `g ↦ g + ε f_i` is reversed by the step `-ε f_i`.
nodes.title: Moves can be undone

nodes.summary: `h` is obtained from the table `g` by adding or subtracting one of the moves `f i` and is again a table of nonnegative counts (Diaconis–Sturmfels 1998, condition (1.5b) with a single move).
nodes.title: One step of the moves chain

nodes.summary: `f⁻(x) = max(-f(x), 0)`, so that `f = f⁺ - f⁻` with disjoint supports (Diaconis–Sturmfels 1998, Section 3.1).
nodes.title: Negative part of an integer move

nodes.summary: `f⁺(x) = max(f(x), 0)` (Diaconis–Sturmfels 1998, Section 3.1).
nodes.title: Positive part of an integer move

nodes.summary: `T` viewed with values in `ℤ^d`.
nodes.title: Integer form of a sufficient statistic

nodes.summary: For `T : X → ℕ^d`, the additive map sending a table of counts `a : X →₀ ℕ` to `∑_x a(x) T(x) ∈ ℕ^d`: the sufficient statistic `t` of Diaconis–Sturmfels (1998), equation (1.3), whose fibres are the sets `F_t` of data sets with the same sufficient statistic.
nodes.title: Sufficient-statistic map of a toric model

nodes.summary: The coordinatewise cast `ℕ^X → ℤ^X`.
nodes.title: A table of counts as an integer vector

nodes.summary: Over any field `k`, the kernel of the monomial map `k[X] → k[t_1, …, t_d]`, `x ↦ t^{T(x)}`, is the ideal generated by the binomials `x^a - x^b` whose exponent vectors have the same sufficient statistic, `∑ a(x) T(x) = ∑ b(x) T(x)`.
nodes.title: Toric ideals are generated by binomials

nodes.summary: The kernel `I_T` of the monomial map `x ↦ t^{T(x)}` (Diaconis–Sturmfels 1998, Section 3.1).
nodes.title: Toric ideal

nodes.summary: `φ_T (c x^a) = c t^{∑ a(x) T(x)}`.
nodes.title: The monomial map on a monomial

nodes.summary: The `k`-algebra map `φ_T : k[X] → k[t_1, …, t_d]` sending each variable `x` to the monomial `t^{T(x)}` (Diaconis–Sturmfels 1998, Section 3.1).
nodes.title: Monomial map of a toric model

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
